name: TLE2081 / TLE2082 / TLE2084 (TI Excalibur high-speed JFET-input)
tagline: A fast (40 V/us, 10 MHz, up to 38 V supply) TI JFET-input op-amp that Head-Fi CMoy builders called a lively, clean, detailed budget pick.
technology: BiFET. The input is a P-channel JFET differential pair: both TI PSpice macromodels (level 1 and level 2) use PJF devices J1/J2, and TI's product folders call it a 'JFET-input operational amplifier'. Part of TI's 'Excalibur' TLE20xx generation. Rev B of the datasheet said the family has more than twice the bandwidth and three times the slew rate of the TL07x/TL08x, with supply rails up to ±19 V. Rev C (Mar 2026) dropped 'JFET-Input' from the document title and removed 'BiFET' from the Features list; see silicon_changes. Made as a single (TLE2081), dual (TLE2082) and quad (TLE2084), each also in a tighter-offset A grade. Older datasheets also list Y chip (die) forms.

reputation.summary: This is a niche, budget-tier favourite rather than a legend. Head-Fi CMoy/portable-amp threads (c. 2007–2009) group it with its sister TLE2072 among good cheap op-amps for 9 V CMoys. Users there say the TLE2072 has the better DC specs and the TLE2082 the better AC specs, and describe the TLE2082 as 'lively, clean, detailed' and good for budget builds. No published distortion or noise measurement (ASR, Samuel Groner, diyAudio) was found, and none was searched for in this session.
typical_uses: 9 V battery CMoy headphone amplifiers (op-amp rolling)
Input/gain stage and driver for discrete-transistor headphone output stages, e.g. the ohdsp AmpTwo (2017): TLE2082 input stage, TLE2081 driving BCP53/BCP56
General fast JFET-input buffering and filtering, e.g. the SampleScope oscilloscope front end
Proposed as a replacement for the MC33182D in the Gameboy DSO project
caveats: The evidence base is small: a handful of Head-Fi CMoy threads, with no documented measurements.
JFET-input noise (about 11.6 nV/rtHz typ, per a model library) is well above bipolar audio op-amps such as the NE5532 (about 5 nV/rtHz). This matters in low-impedance or high-gain stages.
Output current is about 25 mA (LISO library), so low-impedance headphones need a buffer or discrete output stage.
It is fast (10 MHz, 40 V/us). As general engineering caution, not a documented report: use short decoupling and watch capacitive loads when rolling it into circuits designed for TL07x-class parts.
The praise dates from c.2007–09. If TI changed the die around the 2026 datasheet revision (unconfirmed), new-production parts may not match those reports.

revision_history.changes: Original TLE2082/TLE2082A/TLE2082Y dual-only datasheet. The date comes from the rev A header 'AUGUST 1991 – REVISED AUGUST 1994'.
Revision of the dual datasheet (37 pages); changes not seen.
Combined TLE208x/TLE208xA/TLE208xY datasheet covering single, dual and quad. That it superseded SLOS105 is inferred.
Existence implied by the B letter; not seen.
Header 'FEBRUARY 1997 – REVISED JUNE 2001'. Title: 'TLE208x, TLE208xA, TLE208xY EXCALIBUR HIGH-SPEED JFET-INPUT OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS'. Changes not seen.

Moved to the modern TI format with new numbering of tables, figures and cross-references. Removed 'BiFET' and the slew-rate details from Features, and deleted 'On-chip offset voltage trimming'. Added an Applications section, changed the Description, and added a single-pole low-pass filter figure. The title became 'TLE208x and TLE208xA Excalibur High-Speed Operational Amplifiers', dropping JFET-Input and the Y chip forms.
Legacy typeset titled 'TLE208x, TLE208xA, TLE208xY Excalibur High-Speed JFET-Input Operational Amplifiers'. The change content was not shown.

Rewritten in the modern TI format ('1 Features' section) and retitled 'TLE208x and TLE208xA Excalibur High-Speed Operational Amplifiers'. The TLE208xY variants are no longer in the title. The detailed changes were not shown.

Dual-only datasheet 'EXCALIBUR HIGH-SPEED JFET-INPUT DUAL OPERATIONAL AMPLIFIERS' (TLE2082, TLE2082A, TLE2082Y), 37 pages. The summary quoted these specs: 28 V/us minimum slew rate, 10 MHz typical and 8 MHz minimum GBW, 1.5 mA typical supply current per channel, Vos maximum 7 mV (TLE2082) and 4 mV (TLE2082A), and +/-2.25 V to +/-19 V supply. The list of changes from the August 1991 original was not shown.

The search summaries confirm the header 'SLOS182B - FEBRUARY 1997 - REVISED JUNE 2001'. The description claims more than twice the bandwidth (10 MHz) and three times the slew rate (45 V/us) of the TL07x/TL08x BiFET families, rails to +/-19 V, and on-chip zener trimming of offset voltage for the precision (A) grades. The change list from revision A was not shown.

silicon_changes.summary: TI PCN 20231219013.1 moves TLE208x orderables to RFAB with a die revision and an assembly-site change; the die was changed as a result of the process change. Datasheet Rev C (March 2026) later removed 'BiFET', the slew-rate bullet and 'On-chip offset voltage trimming' from Features, rewrote the Description and dropped 'JFET-Input' from the title. TI made the same kind of edits in the refreshes that followed new dies on the TL07x. Linking the Rev C edits to the PCN die is an inference, and no electrical deltas were retrieved.

counterfeit_notes: No TLE208x-specific counterfeit or remarking reports were found, and no dedicated search was run. It is a low-volume, inexpensive TI part and an unlikely main counterfeit target. Treat 'TLE2082' DIPs from marketplace sellers as unverified and prefer authorized distributors. Quick bench check: slew rate should be about 40 V/us typ and input bias current tens of pA at room temperature. A remarked TL072/TL082 would slew only about 13 V/us.

open_questions: Does SLOS182 rev C (Mar 2026) reflect a new die or process? Its Features dropped BiFET and on-chip offset trimming. Compare rev C and rev B electrical tables (noise, Vos, slew, Iq) and look for a TI PCN.
The date and content of SLOS182A, and of the original SLOS105 (Aug 1991), were not seen.
Did the TLE2081 and TLE2084 have their own datasheets before 1997?

revision_chain_notes:
Texas Instruments is the only vendor; no second source, acquirer re-issue or licensed copy turned up. The revision chain from oldest to newest:

(1) SLOS105, the dual-only TLE2082/TLE2082A/TLE2082Y datasheet. The original edition is dated August 1991, but no copy was found; it is known only from the rev A header. Rev A, dated August 1994, is held on alldatasheet (known 184217, plus new page views 184218 and 184222 of the same 37-page document). Missing: the August 1991 original, and any rev B if one exists.

(2) SLOS182, the combined TLE2081/TLE2082/TLE2084 datasheet. The original edition is dated February 1997, and no copy was identified. Rev A is not seen; its date is unknown (between Feb 1997 and Jun 2001), and searches for 'SLOS182A' found nothing. Rev B, dated June 2001, is confirmed by the header 'FEBRUARY 1997 - REVISED JUNE 2001' in the search summaries. The search index still gives ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tle2082.pdf the legacy B title, so a Wayback capture of that URL or its focus.ti.com equivalent before 2026 should hold rev B. Rev C, dated March 2026, is the current ti.com symlink. Missing: copies of the SLOS182 original and rev A.

New third-party copies of SLOS182 do not show their revision: alldatasheet 28971 and 28972, datasheetspdf 1442206, datasheet4u 1442209 and 1442212, radiolocman di=82971, datasheetcatalog TLE2082, the datasheetarchive index pages, and manualmachine 5854290. The most likely places to find the missing 1991 original, the 1997 original and SLOS182A are the older third-party mirrors (datasheetcatalog, datasheetarchive, radiolocman 82971, manualmachine tle2082y).

The archive_seed_urls on focus.ti.com and www-s.ti.com/sc/ds were built from TI's known legacy URL patterns for the Wayback lookup. None of them appeared in a search result, so none is verified.
